Index series to a base period (wrapper around tsbox::ts_index())

index_to_base.Rd

Sets each series to base_value in the base period and scales the rest of the series by the same factor. Formerly index(), renamed because it masked zoo::index() and xts::index(); then ts_rebase() in fcutils 0.1.0 (the ts_ prefix is tsbox's) and rebase() in 0.1.1 and 0.1.2 (rebasing re-expresses a real series in the prices of another year, which this function does not do).

Usage

index_to_base(x, base_per, base_value = 100)

Arguments

x

ts-boxable object to be indexed

base_per

base period, in any form to_ymd() reads. With one date, the first observation on or after it equals base_value, so 2019 sets 2019Q1 (or January 2019) to base_value. With two dates, the mean of the observations from the first date to the second equals base_value. A date stands for the first day of its period, so c(2019.1, 2019.4) covers 2019 for quarterly data, and monthly data need c("2019-01-01", "2019-12-31").

base_value

numeric value of the index at base_per (e.g. 1 or 100)

Value

indexed object of the same type as the input

Examples

jobs <- conv_xts(quarterly_data_example)[, c("E_NF_HI", "ECT_HI")]
# 2010Q1 = 100
round(index_to_base(jobs, 2010.1)[p(2010.1, 2010.4)], 2)
#>            E_NF_HI ECT_HI
#> 2010-01-01  100.00 100.00
#> 2010-04-01  100.19  98.08
#> 2010-07-01  100.29  96.48
#> 2010-10-01  100.89  97.83
# the average of 2010 = 100
idx <- index_to_base(jobs, c(2010.1, 2010.4))
round(idx[p(2010.1, 2010.4)], 2)
#>            E_NF_HI ECT_HI
#> 2010-01-01   99.66 101.94
#> 2010-04-01   99.85  99.98
#> 2010-07-01   99.95  98.35
#> 2010-10-01  100.54  99.72
colMeans(idx[p(2010.1, 2010.4)])
#> E_NF_HI  ECT_HI 
#>     100     100 
# the same with dates, and 1 as the base value
round(index_to_base(jobs, c("2010-01-01", "2010-12-31"), 1)[p(2010.1, 2010.4)], 4)
#>            E_NF_HI ECT_HI
#> 2010-01-01  0.9966 1.0194
#> 2010-04-01  0.9985 0.9998
#> 2010-07-01  0.9995 0.9835
#> 2010-10-01  1.0054 0.9972
